items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We had also engaged a young French musician from Toulouse, Guy Lafitte... Benny fitted into the band very well... Guy Lafitte was playing tenor, so I didn't need another one.

ctx.x: Dickie Wells arrived in Paris the 6th of October, 1952. I went to meet him at the station with Charles Delaunay. Dickie had forgot his coat in New York and the weather was quite bad, the day he arrived, so he was freezing.

We started rehearsals the next day. We had also engaged a young French musician from Toulouse, Guy Lafitte. He was 21 years old and played the tenor and clarinet. The previous year, he had made a concert with Mez Mezrow and Zutty and had got good reviews from the jazz critics.

Arstella Whitthers, who meanwhile on the suggestion of Lily, had changed her name for the pseudonyme of Martine Kay, had been engaged for the tour. But a few weeks before, she wrote that she was ill and could not make the tour. Lily tried to get in touch with her immediately as we had started to advertise her, but she couldn't be found nowhere. What had happened was that the girl had fallen in love and would not leave her boy friend for several months. Lily was very sore for business reasons and also because…
